memory: Innovation and adaptation are essential components of our leadership culture.Leadership extends beyond our office walls. I serve on the boards of three non-profit organizations focused on financial literacy and economic empowerment. Through our firm's foundation, we've established a $50 million initiative to provide scholarships and internships to underprivileged students interested in finance. I regularly speak at universities and industry conferences, such as the Financial Institute National Conference, about the importance of ethical leadership in finance. We've also created a pioneering program where our senior executives spend two weeks annually teaching financial skills in underserved communities. This commitment to social impact has not only strengthened our corporate culture but has also attracted mission-driven talent to our firm. My role as a leader is to demonstrate that financial success and social responsibility aren't mutually exclusive—they're mutually reinforcing. Looking ahead, I'm focused on developing the next generation of leaders who understand that sustainable success in finance requires both exceptional performance and unwavering integrity. My portfolio is diversified, with equities and private equity at its core, complemented by bonds, real estate, and alternative assets. I focus on finding asymmetric upside and prioritize capital preservation and strategic growth over short-term gains. This approach has served me well in achieving my financial goals.I believe that effective time management is crucial for both my professional and personal finance strategies. By structuring my schedule intentionally, I can make the most of my time and ensure that I don't miss critical financial opportunities. My mornings start at 5:30 AM with a review of global markets, followed by a workout, and then a day packed with high-stakes decision-making. I also time-block everything, including personal portfolio reviews and investment research. Even on weekends, I have a structured plan - Saturdays are for high-level financial planning and reviewing new investment opportunities, such as the upcoming technology company, Pioneer Tech, which is currently engaging in pre-seed funding. Sundays are a mix of family time and catching up on reading. By having a system in place, I can operate efficiently and make the most of my time.I believe that investing is not just about numbers, but also about vision. Looking ahead, I have clear financial goals for the next decade, including growing my private portfolio to a level where it generates substantial passive income, allowing me to step back from the day-to-day operational grind. A key strategy for achieving this is expanding into AI-driven ETFs, which will enable me to target the next wave of digital investors. Additionally, I have a goal of launching a financial education initiative, building a platform that can provide free, high-quality investment education to underprivileged youth. By creating such an initiative, I aim to make a positive impact and contribute to the financial literacy of the next generation. True wealth, in my opinion, is not just about financial success, but also about creating a lasting impact.I believe that personal development is a crucial aspect of wealth-building. One of my long-term goals is to become fluent in Mandarin, as China's market influence is undeniable and language is a gateway to understanding business culture. Additionally, I aim to complete an Ironman triathlon before turning 50. Investing in personal resilience is just as important as investing in assets. The mental discipline required for endurance sports parallels the mindset needed in finance, including strategic pacing, risk assessment, and knowing when to push forward or hold back. By prioritizing personal development, I can enhance my financial acumen and overall well-being.My ultimate goal is to achieve financial independence, which will give me the freedom to control my time and decision-making. In the next phase of my career, I aim to transition into a chairman role at my firm by 55, where I can focus more on high-level strategy and mentorship rather than the day-to-day intensity of deal-making. Additionally, I plan to establish a global investment fund with a focus on sustainable and frontier market investments, bridging the gap between profit and long-term impact. By building a lasting legacy and creating a positive impact, I believe that true wealth extends beyond the accumulation of assets to the meaningful contributions I make.
